items.stem: What does LoRA change during fine-tuning to save memory and compute?

options.text: It trains small low-rank update matrices while freezing the base weights
options.rationale: Correct: LoRA learns low-rank deltas and keeps base weights frozen.

options.text: It retrains all base weights at higher precision
options.rationale: That is full fine-tuning, the opposite of LoRA.

options.text: It deletes layers from the model

options.rationale: LoRA adapts weights, not the tokenizer.

items.explanation: Correct: LoRA learns low-rank deltas and keeps base weights frozen.

items.stem: Which TWO are advantages of parameter-efficient fine-tuning over full fine-tuning? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Much lower memory and storage per task
options.rationale: Correct: only small adapter weights are trained and stored.

options.text: Easier to serve many task-specific adapters from one base
options.rationale: Correct: adapters can be swapped on a shared base.

options.text: It always reaches higher accuracy than full tuning
options.rationale: PEFT may trail full tuning on some tasks.

options.text: It removes the need for any training data

items.explanation: Correct: only small adapter weights are trained and stored.

items.stem: Why can setting the LoRA rank much higher than necessary be wasteful?

options.text: It adds trainable parameters and cost with little accuracy gain
options.rationale: Correct: beyond a point extra rank gives diminishing returns.
Rank does not control base-weight freezing.
A higher rank is still trainable, just costlier.
